items.description: Upper River Derwent, Stonethwaite Beck and Derwent Water
items.message:
High river levels today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible on Saturday 10 October .
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers including Keswick Campsite. The lake levels will stay elevated for most of today, Saturday 10th of October. We are not expecting any property flooding.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Sunday 11 October or as the situation changes.

Strong winds and large waves this evening may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 17:15pm to 21:15pm on Saturday 10th October
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at  King's Lynn of 3.97mAODN at 19:15pm, on 10 October, which is  0.12m above tide tables, Wind Force 7,  Westerly. The high tide tomorrow at 07:15am is expected to also be above flood alert thresholds.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 9:00PM on Saturday 10 October or as the situation changes.

High tides tomorrow evening may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 17:30 to 19:30 on 10/10/2026 
Flooding is forecast to affect locations at Porlock Bay, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around the coastline between Gore Point and Hurlstone Point including Porlock Weir. The highest tide is at 18:30 on Saturday 10/10/2026 with a peak height of 6.19m and a F5 westerly wind. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Sunday 11 October or as the situation changes.

items.description: The Suffolk coast from Lowestoft to Bawdsey
items.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 8:30am to 10:30am on Saturday 10th October. 
We expect to see high water levels in Lake Lothing in Lowestoft, as well as high sea levels along the Suffolk Coast, impacting on beach access points. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Lowestoft of 1.72 mAODN at 9:30am on Saturday 10th October, which is 0.51m above tide tables, Wind Force 6, Westerly. No further high tides are currently expected over the coming days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Saturday 10 October or as the situation changes.
